meta.title: The cost-trap atlas for marketing, sales and e-commerce software (data)
meta.note: A slice of the AIBuilder Marketplace open dataset: the tools covered on marketingandsalessoftware.com. Every flag carries the dossier sentence it rests on.

tools.name: 24-7PressRelease
tools.entry_price_terms: Simple Post · one-off, per release, posted on their own site only
tools.price_note: (read 2026-10-08 on 24-7pressrelease.com/pricing, USD, prices per release) Six plans, each paid per press release rather than by subscription. Simple Post is $29 and adds your news to their own website only, with no additional distribution. Visibility Boost is $49, described as structured regional online distribution. PR Network Plus is $89 and expands digital distribution for regional reach. Integrated Media Pro, marked most popular, is $139 and adds digital and traditional media distribution. Integrated Media Pro+, marked best value, is $199 and extends distribution across US and Canadian media networks. Mass Media Visibility is $479 and is the only plan that names PR Newswire, for national and extended digital distribution. Each plan has a one-line description and a 'View Plan Details' link; the comparison page linked from the pricing page returned 'Page Not Found' when we read it. The site also lists an agency discount program and writing services, without prices on the pricing page. The home page says the service has run since 2004 and promises publication within 24 hours.

tools.name: ActiveCampaign
tools.entry_price_terms: per month billed annually (1 user)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-17 and again 2026-09-29 in the browser; the figures below are the 'starts at' prices on annual billing, before you pick a contact count) No free plan, trial only. There are four tiers. Starter is from $15/mo with 1 user, limited segmentation and 5 actions per automation. Plus is from $49/mo with 1 user, standard segmentation, unlimited automation actions and landing pages. Pro is from $79/mo with 3 users, advanced segmentation, predictive and conditional content and attribution tracking. Enterprise is from $145/mo with 5 users, premium segmentation, SSO, custom objects and a dedicated account team. Your email send allowance is a multiple of your contact count — 10x on Starter and Plus, 12x on Pro, 15x on Enterprise. The bill then scales with list size, and the ladder only renders after you select a contact count: at 10,000 contacts on 2026-09-29 it read Starter $149, Plus $189, Pro $375 and Enterprise $589 a month on annual billing. A separate Email + WhatsApp plan starts at $112 (Plus), $142 (Pro) and $284 (Enterprise) a month, each with up to 5 WhatsApp lines. CRM pipelines, SMS and extra users remain paid add-ons. Read again on 9 October 2026 with the contact selector, billed annually (the page offers no monthly option). Starter $15 at 1,000, $39 at 2,500, $79 at 5,000, $109 at 7,500, $149 at 10,000, $231 at 15,000, $311 at 20,000, $391 at 25,000 contacts, and 'Only available on plans with 25,000 contacts or less'. Plus $49 at 1,000, $95 at 2,500, $145 at 5,000, $169 at 7,500, $189 at 10,000, $265 at 15,000, $329 at 20,000, $389 at 25,000, $449 at 30,000, $549 at 40,000, $609 at 50,000. Pro $79 at 1,000, $149 at 2,500, $205 at 5,000, $289 at 7,500, $375 at 10,000, $465 at 15,000, $549 at 20,000, $629 at 25,000, $709 at 30,000, $879 at 40,000, $969 at 50,000. Enterprise $145 at 1,000, $255 at 2,500, $375 at 5,000, $479 at 7,500, $589 at 10,000, $689 at 15,000, $785 at 20,000, $879 at 25,000, $949 at 30,000, $1,095 at 40,000, $1,169 at 50,000. Above 50,000 contacts the page shows no price.

tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-15, read on their own homepage pricing table) Credit-metered, where one credit is one downloaded creative, and there is no free plan — only a 7-day trial with 10 credits. tools.entry_price_terms: per month minimum on Self-Serve
tools.price_note: (price re-verified 2026-09-10, re-read unchanged 2026-09-27) Read on adwisely.com/pricing; every figure below stood unchanged from our previous reading on 2 August 2026. Both plans charge 10% of the ad spend Adwisely manages, with a monthly minimum that acts as a floor rather than a fee on top: $49 on Self-Serve and $249 on Concierge (managed). At $5,000 of monthly spend the Self-Serve fee is therefore $500, not $549, and total monthly Adwisely fees are capped at $3,250 (re-read 15 September 2026). 7-day free trial, no setup fee.

tools.name: AfterSell
tools.entry_price_terms: a month at 200 monthly orders, capped at $999.99
tools.price_note: Three plans, each metered by monthly order volume, read on aftersell.com/pricing and on the Shopify App Store listing on 22 September 2026 (re-verified 22 September 2026 and again 27 September 2026). The entry prices: Post-Purchase $34.99 a month for 200 monthly orders, capped at $999.99; Pre-Purchase $59.99 for 200, capped at $599.99; Complete $79.99, capped at $1,359.99 - and on 27 September 2026 the Complete card quotes that $79.99 for 500 monthly orders, where on 22 September it read 200 like the other two. The page does not say whether the Complete entry tier was widened or the card is wrong, so confirm the tier for your own volume in the app before you install. Complete is the other two together, which the vendor prices at 15% under buying them separately. Go over a volume tier and the fee steps up to the matching one on its own, with that cap as the ceiling. Every plan carries a 30-day free trial, all charges are billed in USD, and the Free plan on the listing is for development and partner stores only. Checkout upsells are Shopify Plus only and now sit inside Post-Purchase and Complete rather than being billed separately. Rokt Thanks, the third-party offers on the confirmation page, is free with no minimum order volume and pays up to $0.80 per order; for stores above 1,000 monthly orders whose primary market is the US, Canada, Australia or the UK those earnings are credited against the subscription dollar for dollar. Aftersell Max, for high-volume stores, is custom-priced and publishes no figure. The unexplained $19.99 we saw above the $79.99 on the Complete card on 22 September 2026 is no longer on the page on 27 September. This replaces the single order-volume ladder we recorded on 5 September 2026 ($34.99 for 0-500 orders, $54.99 for 501-1,000, $99.99 for 1,001-2,000); that ladder is on neither page any more.

flags.evidence: Three plans, each metered by monthly order volume, read on aftersell.com/pricing and on the Shopify App Store listing on 22 September 2026 (re-verified 22 September 2026 and again 27 September 2026).

tools.name: AgentNest
tools.entry_price_terms: Starter · per month for 100 successful automated fixes, billed in USD every 30…
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-10-09 on apps.shopify.com/agentnest; first read 2026-08-19, no amount or allowance changed in between, though the listing now calls the app 'AgentNest - ChatGPT Ad Catalog' and pitches the scan as preparation for ChatGPT Ads) Four tiers, and the split between them is unusual: the diagnosis is free and you pay only for the repairs. Free: unlimited catalogue scans, a catalogue readiness score, product-level issue reports and the full findings view. Starter $19 a month: 100 successful automated fixes a month, one-click fixes for all eligible issues, product-level recommendations. Growth $49 a month: 1,000 fixes a month, revenue-priority catalogue insights, fix history and progress tracking. Scale $99 a month: 5,000 fixes a month, advanced revenue-priority insights and bulk catalogue fixes. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days, and no tier shows a free trial. The billing unit is a 'successful automated fix', and the listing never defines it. Whether one fix is one product, one field on one product, or one alt text on one image is the difference between $19 covering a hundred products and a hundred images. It is also the only variable separating the three paid tiers. Developer Ecommerce Storez, 1255 23rd St NW, Washington DC; the app launched on 6 August 2026 and has no reviews at all.

tools.name: Aira
tools.entry_price_terms: a month, billed annually (€5,988 a year)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-10-15 on aira.app/pricing; first read in this form 2026-10-10) Aira now sells one product on its pricing page: Aira Connect at €499 a month, billed annually (€5,988 a year). That includes all 14 markets, unlimited users, every CRM integration (HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive and MS Dynamics), API and MCP access, and 1,000 companies synced to your CRM. Above that the page prints a flat rate: €28 a month per extra 1,000 companies from 1,001 to 50,000, and 'Contact sales' above 50,000 (read 15 October 2026; on 10 October we did not see the amount). The €149 per user a month plan we read in July and August is no longer on the pricing page, the homepage or the about page. A 5-day free trial is offered. Prices are in euros.

tools.name: AISDR
tools.entry_price_terms: per person contacted (charged daily, no subscription)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-10-15 on aisdr.com/pricing and AiSDR's plain-text pricing reference for AI assistants, aisdr.com/pricing-for-llms, marked 'Last updated: 2026-10-15') AiSDR has replaced its published plan ladder with two routes. Pay as you go: $1.50 per person contacted, charged daily for the people contacted that day, with no subscription, no monthly fee, no contract and no sales call. You pick a pace of 5, 10 or 20 people a day, which the page itself works out as $7.50, $15 or $30 a day, and research, lists and writing are included in the $1.50. The reference says campaigns start from as little as $3; another FAQ on the main pricing page says from $7.50. Team plans are for teams contacting 1,000+ people a month: priced on volume with 'up to 40% lower price per contact', no amount published, billed monthly from the day you sign up on a quarterly or annual contract, with annual 20% cheaper than quarterly. Each team plan includes a monthly contact limit; extra contacts are bought in the app at a price the page does not publish. Add-ons: warmed-up mailbox $33 per mailbox setup, per-campaign managed service $149 per campaign, fully managed service $2,500 per month. Historical: until at least 11 October 2026 AiSDR published Solo at $250/mo, Explore at $900/mo and Scale at $2,500/mo; none of those plans appears on either page on 15 October 2026.

tools.name: Algomo
tools.entry_price_terms: a month (no per-seat pricing)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-10-03 on newmode.ai/pricing and the homepage) Plans start at $200 a month with no per-seat pricing - and that single sentence is still the entire public price list, unchanged since our July and August readings and again on 14 September and 3 October 2026. The pricing page carries exactly two plans, Growth and Enterprise, and both buttons say 'Let's chat' and 'Book call': no amount, no contact slider, no self-serve tier. Growth lists 1:1 personalized LinkedIn ads, AI-generated ad copy, website personalization, CRM integration and email support; Enterprise adds unlimited campaigns, custom integrations, a dedicated success manager, priority support and advanced analytics. What drives the price between the two is not published anywhere on the site, so the only figure a buyer can budget against is the $200 floor.

tools.name: Alidrop
tools.entry_price_terms: per month (50 unique/25 premium products)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-10-02 on their own pricing page) Four monthly plans: Starter $39/mo (50 unique / 25 premium products), Professional $59/mo (500 unique / 250 premium), Empire $99/mo (5,000 unique / 2,500 premium) and Unicorn $299/mo (25,000 unique / 25,000 premium). A 7-day trial costs $1, and there are no transaction or hidden fees. Annual billing is listed only from Professional up — $288, $684 and $948 a year — and the discount grows with the tier: 6 months off Professional, 5 off Empire and 8 off Unicorn, so the advertised “up to 8 months off” is the Unicorn rate rather than a general one, and Starter has no annual column at all. An optional one-time custom-store build service starts at $299. The $1 trial converts to the full monthly rate of whichever plan you picked, and your card stays on file — set a reminder if you are only testing.

tools.price_note: (prices re-verified 2026-09-19 on alliai.com/pricing) Billed in USD, no free tier, a 10-day free trial on every plan and cancellation from the dashboard at any time. The page shows two ladders behind a Monthly/Annual toggle. Paid monthly: Business $299 a month (5 sites, 5 team members, 500 keywords, 1,250 pages) and Agency $599 a month (15 sites, 15 team members, 2,000 keywords, 5,000 pages). Paid annually: Business $2,990 a year and Agency $5,990 a year, which the page prints as $249 and $499 a month, a saving of $598 and $1,198 respectively. Enterprise is quote-only (50 sites, 50 team members, 5,000 keywords, 20,000 pages). Every quota has a published add-on price that differs per tier and per term: monthly Business is extra sites from $39 each, extra keywords from $24.99 per 100 and extra pages from $14.99 per 250; annual Business $32.50, $20.83 and $12.50; monthly Agency $29, $14.99 and $9.99; annual Agency $24.17, $12.50 and $8.33. Business and Agency carry the same engine — the AI Search Visibility Engine, pre-rendering for 50-plus AI crawlers, the AI bot traffic monitor, LLM Mode, keyword tracking, site speed optimizer, link builder, standard reports and a weekly crawl — and Agency adds only API access, white label and snippet hosting.

tools.name: AltText.ai
tools.entry_price_terms: per month (100 credits/mo)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 10 Oct 2026; figures unchanged since 26 Aug 2026) Credit-metered — one credit = one image. Free trial: 25 credits, no credit card required. Monthly: Bronze $5/mo (100 credits/mo, 5¢ per image), Silver $19/mo (500), Gold $59/mo (2,000), Titanium $119/mo (5,000), Platinum $229/mo (10,000). Annual buys the same yearly credit volume at a discount the page labels 17-31% off: $49/yr (1,200 credits), $189/yr (6,000), $489/yr (24,000), $1,179/yr (60,000), $2,199/yr (120,000). One-time credit packs are 50 credits for $3 with no subscription; beyond 120,000 credits a year is custom enterprise pricing. Unused plan credits roll over when the plan renews on its normal cycle, and banked rollover credits and one-time packs stay in the account — but the FAQ states that changing plans, up or down, forfeits the current period’s unused plan credits. You can cancel anytime and keep what is unused, and every feature ships on every plan. Two multipliers change the real per-image cost: advanced formats (AVIF, HEIC, HEIF, JP2, SVG, TIFF) bill 2 credits and are paid-plans-only, and each additional translation language costs 1 more credit per image.

tools.name: Amplemarket
tools.entry_price_terms: per month billed annually (2 users)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-09-14) The only published price is Startup at $600/mo on an annual term, covering 2 users, with additional users available to purchase; Growth and Elite are listed as Custom, so those numbers come from sales rather than the site. All plans include a free trial. Startup covers 13,500 email address credits and 600 phone number credits per user per year, 2 mailboxes per user and 27,000 contacts. Growth lists 4 users, 35,000 email and 5,000 phone credits per user per year, 4 mailboxes and 140,000 contacts. Elite lists 10 users, 40,000 email and 9,600 phone credits, 8 mailboxes and 400,000 contacts. Two gated rows are easy to miss in the comparison table and both start at zero or near it on Startup: Custom Data Requests run 0, 4 and 12 per plan, so a Startup customer cannot ask for a bespoke data pull at all, and Job Change Alerts cover 500, 1,000 and 2,000 contacts. Duo Inbox is marked as an Add-On rather than an included feature, and the MCP row - prospecting and taking action from inside Claude or ChatGPT - is listed as a platform feature with no plan boundary stated.

tools.name: Atria
tools.entry_price_terms: a month, billed annually (a stated $360/yr saving), 5 seats
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-17 and 2026-10-07 on their own pricing page, annual billing, which Atria advertises as 20% off) Core is $129/mo, a stated $360 saving a year. That covers 5 seats, 4,000 AI credits a month, 50 brands followed without AI insights, 5 connected ad accounts, $500K of ad spend analysed a month, 5GB of asset storage and 3 brand profiles. Plus $479/mo (a stated $1,440 saving): 8 seats, 10,000 credits, 100 brands with AI insights, 10 ad accounts, $1M of ad spend, 1TB storage, 8 brand profiles. Business $959/mo (a stated $2,880 saving): 15 seats, 25,000 credits, 200 brands with AI insights, unlimited ad accounts and ad spend. Enterprise is custom. Extra seats are $20 each a month on every tier. Note the step from Core to Plus is far steeper than the tier names suggest — it is roughly 3.7x the price for 2.5x the credits. Billed monthly, read 7 October 2026: Core $159, Plus $599, Business $1,199. Against those monthly rates annual billing saves 18.9% on Core ($360 a year) and 20.0% on Plus and Business, so the 'Save 20%' label is slightly generous on Core. Core also includes 600 MCP calls and 1,200 REST API calls a month, and each call over the cap costs 1 AI credit; on Plus and above both are unlimited.

tools.entry_price_terms: ReCapture · minimum per month

tools.name: Bitscale
tools.entry_price_terms: per month for 15,000 (Booster $799 for 50,000)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 13 September 2026 on bitscale.ai/pricing, extended on 11 September 2026 from inside a free account; every headline figure unchanged since 1 September 2026) The meter is credits. Free is $0 with 200 credits, no card required, capped at 20 action columns per grid and 50,000 rows. Growth is $349 a month for 15,000 credits, 30 action columns and 100,000 rows, with a two-way HubSpot integration and inbound integrations like RB2B, Factors and Vector. Booster is $799 for 50,000 credits and 50 action columns, adding curated scraping scripts, a private Slack channel and Salesforce integration. Enterprise is quote-only but publishes a floor most vendors hide: annual billing at $15,000 and above, adding SOC 2 and SSO, priority support, role-based team access and Snowflake pipelines. Annual billing takes 10% off. Two lines in the plan table change the arithmetic and are easy to miss. Credits roll over up to three times the plan allowance on Growth and Booster, and not at all on Free, so a quiet month is banked rather than lost. And a credit is spent only when a data provider returns a valid result -- the pricing FAQ says failed lookups, formula columns and CRM syncs are always free -- so a waterfall that finds nothing costs nothing. The page also contradicts itself twice: the comparison table gives all four tiers 100+ data sources while the Free card says 10+ B2B data sources, and the Growth and Booster cards both promise Unlimited Actions while the same page's table caps action columns per grid at 30 and 50. The step from Free to Growth is still the one to plan for: 200 credits to 15,000 with nothing in between, so the bill goes from nothing to $4,188 a year in one move. Monthly company and people search is metered separately at 2,000 on Free, 15,000 on Growth and 50,000 on Booster. Two things the pricing page does not tell you, both read on 11 September 2026. First, what a credit actually buys: Bitscale's own credit documentation prices a found email or phone number at one to twelve platform credits per successful result, depending on how many providers the waterfall is allowed to try, with an AI enrichment at one to two credits a run and a BitAgent website scrape at one. Calls that come in through the API cost nothing. Second, the free tier runs two meters rather than one, and the account screen shows both: 200 platform credits for enrichment and a separate 2,000 search credits for Find People and Find Companies, each resetting monthly. The upgrade panel inside the product also carries a Growth benefit the plan cards leave out -- three hours a quarter with a GTM engineer -- and states plainly what Free locks: credit rollover, more than 20 action columns per grid, the 100+ providers and the inbound integrations.

tools.entry_price_terms: a month or €6.33 billed yearly
tools.price_note: Brevo serves a different price list depending on where you open the page, and the two are not each other's conversion: Starter and Standard differ by more than the exchange rate ($9 and $18 against €7 and €15), while Professional lands on the same 499 in both. Both ladders are below, each with the date it was read. Read on brevo.com/pricing on 6 September 2026 with the currency switched to US dollars and the yearly tab open: Free at $0 with 300 emails a day; Starter from $9 a month for 5,000 emails, or $8.08 on yearly billing; Standard from $18 ($16.17 yearly) adding marketing automation and A/B testing; Professional from $499 ($449 yearly, from 150,000 emails) with multi-user access and contact scoring; Enterprise on quote. So a big list you rarely mail still needs the send tier that stores it. Re-verified 19 September 2026 in a browser, this time in the euro view the page serves from the Netherlands and with the plan builder open: Starter €7 a month or €6.33 on yearly billing (the toggle is labelled -10%), Standard €15 or €13.50, Professional €499 or €449.08 with 10 seats included, and Free unchanged at 300 emails a day once Brevo has approved the account for sending. tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-09-14 on their own pricing page; both billing terms read from the page markup, and no figure has moved since our August reading) Clay meters two things separately — actions and data credits — and each paid plan is an expandable volume rather than a fixed tier, which is the part most write-ups still get wrong, ours included until the August 2026 update. Data credits are a separate meter again — monthly from $125 for 2,500 credits up to $2,125 for 50,000, or annually from $113/mo for 30,000 a year up to $1,913/mo for 600,000. Annual billing saves 10%. Waterfall enrichment spends credits per lookup, so the credit meter rather than the plan is what decides the bill. Read that structure the right way round: the monthly fee is not what you are buying, it is what you pay to lower the per-ticket rate, so the correct plan follows from your ticket volume and nothing else. The crossings are exact. Lite and Growth cost the same at 76 tickets a month; below that Lite wins. Growth and Standard cross at 120. Standard and Professional cross at 560. So a store selling 300 tickets a month pays $199 on Standard against $244 on Growth and $264 on Professional -- the middle tier, and the store's own Popular label happens to be right for that range. One feature line changes that arithmetic and sits above the crossover: Collect fees on every ticket sold appears on Standard and Professional only, so passing the per-ticket cost to attendees is itself a paid feature. Beyond that, feature differences barely enter into it until Professional, which is where reserved seating, Klaviyo and Mailchimp integrations, the multi-vendor dashboard and priority support live. (read 21 September 2026 on www.gushwork.ai/pricing) Gushwork publishes one number and no ladder. The page states “Pricing starts at $900 /month”, billed monthly, cancel anytime, and the FAQ on the same page repeats it: “$900 is the starting point, with every agent and feature switched on.” Everything above that rung is quoted rather than published — “Talk to us, and we’ll recommend the right plan based on your business, goals, and lead potential” — and the FAQ names the three things that move the figure: how many pages you want published, how fast you want to grow, and how much paid support you add, with the exact number confirmed on a call.

The contract says something the pricing page does not. Gushwork's Master Services Terms, version 3.0, effective 31 July 2026 and read on 14 October 2026, give an agreement an initial term of twelve months that renews automatically for further twelve-month periods unless either side gives notice at least 30 days before it ends. tools.name: Kartra
tools.entry_price_terms: a month, or $52 a month billed yearly
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-09-05 and again 2026-09-30 on their own pricing page) Four tiers, monthly against yearly: Essentials $59 / $52, Starter $119 / $99, Growth $229 / $189 and Professional $549 / $429, with yearly billing advertised as saving up to 22% and a 14-day trial. The tier names moved since our August reading — the $119 plan is now called Starter and the $229 plan Growth — while every amount stayed the same. The line that changes the arithmetic and is missing from most summaries: Essentials charges a 5% transaction fee on your sales, and the tiers above it charge 0%. On $10,000 a month of sales that fee is $500, which makes the $60 step from Essentials to Starter trivially worth taking. Contacts are capped at 500, 2,500, 12,500 and 25,000 across the four tiers; Essentials sends 10,000 emails and texts a month against unlimited above it and includes 1 custom domain. Kartra never blocks new leads: it upgrades you automatically to the tier that fits and charges a mid-cycle reconciliation fee for the move — two answers above that one, the same FAQ says a Kartra subscription is flat-rate and there are never any extra fees. On 30 September 2026 all eight amounts were unchanged, and the page now opens with a 30-day money-back guarantee and cancel-anytime line above the plan toggle.

tools.name: Parallel AI
tools.entry_price_terms: per month for 2,000 or $297/mo for 9,000
tools.price_note: (read on 11 September 2026 on parallellabs.app/pricing, which stamps itself 'Last updated: 2026-08-18') The meter is credits, and there are two separate pools. Plan credits come with the subscription: Pay As You Go is $0 with 50 credits and no card, Entrepreneur $99 a month for 2,000 credits and 2 companies, Business $297 for 9,000 credits and 10 companies, and Enterprise is quote-only with SSO, on-premise deployment and dedicated support. Data credits are a different pool, bought once and never expiring, and they are the only part of the product priced per action: 1 data credit per lead or contact returned, 2 per matched enrichment lookup through the API or an agent, and a lookup that finds nothing is free. They run $25 for 500 down to $175 for 5,000, so between 5.0 and 3.5 cents a lead. The two pools expire differently, and the page says so in two places that sit far apart: plan credits 'reset on the 1st of each month', while purchased credit packs and data credits never expire. What the page never says is how many PLATFORM credits an action costs. Content generation, an agent conversation and an outreach step are all simply 'credits' with no published rate, so the 2,000 on Entrepreneur is a quantity without a unit until you have run your own work through it. Per credit the tiers differ by a third: 5.0 cents on Entrepreneur against 3.3 on Business, which is three times the price for four and a half times the credits. Running out has a tier-shaped answer -- the FAQ offers extra credit packages on the Business plan and the Pay-As-You-Go card offers top-ups, but Entrepreneur sits between them with no stated top-up route, so the $99 tier's answer to an empty meter appears to be the $297 one. Seats do not add capacity: every seat in a company shares one monthly pool, and extra seats are $15 a month ($12 annual). The add-ons are where the bill can outgrow the plan -- an extra company is $20 a month ($16 annual), an extra white-label instance $50, and anonymous website pixel identification runs $75, $250 or $500 a month for 500, 2,000 or 5,000 resolutions. On the free tier the limits are real: a 200k context window against 1M on every paid plan, 30 days of chat history instead of unlimited, no App Builder, and model access listed as 'Limited' with response times 'limited on bandwidth and availability'.

tools.name: PartnerStack
tools.price_note:
(read 2026-08-26 on partnerstack.com/pricing) There is no public price at any tier. PartnerStack publishes three plans — Launch, Growth and Enterprise — and every one of them carries a Book your demo button where the number would be; /plans is a 404. What the page does publish is what moves between tiers, and it is unusually specific. Launch gives you affiliate link tracking OR lead and deal registration — you pick one — plus marketplace access, partner payments built for B2B sales cycles, onboarding and enablement tooling, CRM integrations and their AI and MCP connector. Growth adds deeper integration support, a learning-management solution, partner challenges and incentives, MDF management and payments, and segmentation by performance or strategy. Enterprise is the only tier with full access to link tracking AND both registration motions at once, and adds custom workflows, a designated CSM with semi-annual business reviews, partner introductions and priority support. So the ladder the page shows is a ladder of partner motions rather than seats — its FAQ says you can invite as many internal users as you need — and the choice between tracking and registration on the entry tier is the line worth reading twice. The same FAQ adds that the quote itself is based on your partner program size, feature needs and level of support, and is confirmed during the demo.

Re-read on 16 October 2026, together with PartnerStack's standard SaaS Agreement (partnerstack.com/legal/saas-agreement), which says what the pricing page does not. The fee has two parts: an annual Subscription Fee set out in the Order Form and due when you sign, plus a monthly fee calculated as a share of the commissions your partners earn that month, at one rate for partners you bring yourself and another for partners PartnerStack refers to you. Neither rate is published. Unless the Order Form says otherwise, fees are paid in advance in US dollars and cannot be cancelled or refunded, and you also cover the payment provider's transaction costs. The term renews automatically for another year unless either side gives written notice at least 60 days before it ends, and the annual Subscription Fees for a renewal term increase by 7% over the previous period. When the agreement ends you have 30 days to log in and download your data before the account goes inactive. A signed Order Form or addendum overrides these default terms, and the agreement also lets an Order Form set user or usage limits despite the unlimited-users line in the FAQ, so the renewal uplift, the notice window and the commission rates are the three things to get in writing in your own order.

Billing is annual only and Pecan states there is no setup fee. A batch is one run against a dataset, so two a month is a fortnightly cadence — the number that decides your tier before any conversation about team size.

tools.name: Piktochart
tools.entry_price_terms: per member per month billed yearly ($15 monthly)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 6 September and again 19 September 2026 on piktochart.com/pricing/, US dollar view; the plan amounts are unchanged from our 6 August 2026 reading) Free is $0, Pro is $15 per member per month billed monthly or $10 billed annually ($120 a year), Business is $20 monthly or $17 billed annually ($204 a year), and Enterprise is quote-only from 101 members. Free stops at 2 PNG downloads — a flat total, not two a month — 1 GB of storage, 60 AI credits and free templates only, and is capped at four members (one owner plus three). Pro adds unlimited PNG downloads, premium templates and icons, 500 AI credits and 100 GB, and the annual rate is what the page calls 33% off. Business, 15% off annually, adds PDF and PowerPoint export on top of PNG, the Brand Kit (unlimited brand colours, fonts and logos), 1,000 AI credits and 250 GB. Enterprise adds SSO/SAML, workspace management, a dedicated account manager and a one-off hour of training. Three further cards on the same page price other audiences, and two of them beat Pro on both price and capability. Education is $39.99 per member billed annually — the card splits the cents into a separate element, which is why a careless reading gives $39; the FAQ prints the full figure — with 250 AI credits, a limited Brand Kit and unlimited PNG, PDF and PowerPoint downloads, and requires a valid educational email address. Campus is quote-only above 3,000 seats. Nonprofit is $60 per member billed annually with the same 250 credits, limited Brand Kit and unlimited PNG, PDF and PPT downloads. The page's own FAQ calls those two 'a 76% discount' and 'a 64% discount' from its annual pricing, which works back to a list of about $167 a year — a figure that appears nowhere on the page, where annual Pro is $120 and monthly Pro annualises to $180. The page can be switched between USD, GBP, EUR, SGD, MXN and INR. No free trial is offered on the paid tiers — the free plan is the trial — and you can cancel anytime, though the FAQ adds that refunds are generally not given under the Terms of Use and are reviewed case by case, and that purchases of $168 or more can be settled by bank deposit.

tools.name: Post Purchase Upsell Hero
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/post-purchase-upsell-hero and the vendor's own site; amounts unchanged since 31 August, USD) One plan, Performance, free to install, at $0 a month plus usage charges. The usage table, read from the listing's own pricing-estimator data, has two tiers: 2.5% on the first $20,000 of upsell revenue in a month, and $0 from $20,001 up. In practice that is a commission with a ceiling — the app cannot charge more than $500 in a month, and a month in which it sells nothing costs nothing. There is no paid tier above it: unlimited funnels and offers, one-click upsell and downsell, AI product recommendations, analytics and A/B testing and market translations all sit on that single plan. Charges are billed in USD every 30 days. The vendor's own site publishes no prices at all — its pricing link leads to the same single-plan listing — so the listing is the only place the meter is stated. Neither page defined how 'upsell revenue' is measured, so we asked, and the vendor answered in writing on 21 September 2026 with permission to quote it. The figure is net: the amount the customer is actually charged for the accepted upsell item, after any discount set on that offer, and nothing from the original cart is included. Refunds and cancellations of an accepted upsell are reversed automatically through Shopify — proportionally for partial refunds, with the 2.5% coming off alongside, and no support ticket needed — while refunds of original cart items never move the figure, because they were never billed. There is no multi-day attribution window either: the offer exists only on the Shopify post-purchase page between payment and the order confirmation, and the merchant sets how long that moment stays open, with a default of 20 minutes, any value from 1 to 59 minutes, or Shopify's own 60-minute default. The vendor says the full rule now sits in its help center under Pricing and billing. That is the vendor's account of its own meter, dated and on the record, but it is not something we have audited against a live bill.

tools.name: Seller Investigators
tools.price_note: (2026-08-15, read on their own site) One number, and it is the whole model: a 25% commission, charged only after Amazon has deposited recovered funds in your account. We found it stated twice. Once on the home page — “only pay a 25% commission fee when your money is back with you” — and again in the FAQ: “no risk or upfront commitment, with a 25% recovery fee only after Amazon deposits recovered funds into your account”. The audit is free, takes 48 hours and carries no obligation. There is no subscription and no /pricing page, because there is nothing else to price. Cases they say they cover fall into five groups: inbound shipments (cancelled shipments, receiving discrepancies, carrier damage), items lost in transit or in the warehouse, items damaged or disposed of by Amazon, customer returns (refunds not returned within 60 days, overpayments, the wrong item returned, chargebacks), and overages and discrepancies (removal orders, incorrect weights or dimensions, overcharged orders); unfair reimbursement appears as a sub-case under both the lost and the damaged group. Re-read 29 August 2026: the 25% figure, the free 48-hour audit and the absence of any subscription are unchanged. Re-read 11 October 2026 on the home page and FAQ: the 25% commission, the free audit and the absence of a subscription are unchanged; the FAQ adds that the fee applies to all successful refunds including inventory reimbursements, valued at Amazon's per-unit amount, and is negotiable based on the size of the business.

Starter is $100 a month on annual billing only: 1,000 SKUs, one marketplace, one user and up to $15K a month in revenue. Accelerator is $250 month to month or $212 a month paid annually, billed $2,544 a year: the same 1,000 SKUs, three users, up to $30K a month in revenue, and it adds Walmart, Amazon Business B2B repricing and an onboarding specialist. Standard is $500 month to month or $425 a month paid annually, billed $5,100 a year: 15,000 SKUs, three users, no revenue cap, a dedicated account manager and multi-store support. Custom, above Standard, is quote-only. The annual Accelerator rate went up between our September and October readings: it was $175 a month with a $900 yearly saving, and it is now $212 with a saving the page puts at $446 (its own figures give $456). The monthly rates and both Standard figures did not move, so annual billing now takes about 15 percent off Accelerator and Standard alike, where it used to take 30 percent off the smaller plan. What each step buys is still lopsided: Accelerator doubles your revenue ceiling and leaves the SKU count alone, and Standard does the reverse — fifteen times the catalogue with the ceiling removed. So the middle tier is for turnover and the top tier is for range, and a shop that needs neither is paying for the other one. The page now prints the revenue ceilings per month ('Up to $15K/mo revenue'), which matches what Seller Snap told us in writing on 24 Jul 2026. Walmart is no longer on every plan: the Accelerator card reads 'Everything in Starter, plus Walmart, B2B repricing and onboarding specialist'. Every tier carries a 15-day trial with no credit card. tools.entry_price_terms: Basic Plan · per month on the App Store listing, or $67.10 a year, for the checkbox…
tools.price_note:
(read 2026-08-25, re-verified 2026-09-09 and again on 2026-09-29 on apps.shopify.com/terms-and-conditions-checkbox, listed as “TnC: Terms and Conditions Box”, and in the vendor's own pricing article at www.effectify.help) The monthly ladder is $6.99, $10.99 and $12.99, and the annual prices are $67.10, $92.32 and $109.12. The listing puts the annual saving at 20% on Basic and 30% on Advanced and Pro.

This ladder has moved three times in five weeks, each time with the same feature lists. On 24 August 2026 the monthly plans were $6.99, $9.99 and $12.99. On 25 August they were $7.99, $12.99 and $14.99, with annual rates of $67.12, $109.12 and $125.92. By 9 September the annual rates had been cut to $47.94, $77.94 and $89.94 under a “save 50%” label while the monthly ones held. On 29 September both columns had changed again, with the monthly rates back down to $6.99, $10.99 and $12.99. Treat any figure here, ours included, as the price on the day it was read, and check the listing before you install.

Four plans on the listing, and the free one is not for you. Development Stores is free and carries every Pro feature, but the listing states it is for development and partner stores only and that payment will be activated on upgrade — so the “Free plan available” line at the top of the listing describes a partner sandbox rather than a free tier for a store that takes orders. Basic is $6.99 a month or $67.10 a year and covers the AI terms-and-conditions checkbox with support for Buy It Now and express checkout buttons. Advanced is $10.99 a month or $92.32 a year and adds the consent date logged into the order's details plus the ability to show the checkbox for specific countries and products. Pro is $12.99 a month or $109.12 a year and adds newsletter and contact forms, translation of the checkbox into multiple languages, the checkbox in Shopify POS and an AI-powered policies generator. Every paid tier carries a 7-day free trial, and the listing states charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days.

The vendor's own pricing article, re-read on 29 September 2026, now prints the same monthly and annual rates as the listing for all three plans; on 9 September the two pages disagreed on the annual price. The article still puts the annual saving at approximately 30%, which holds for Advanced and Pro and not for Basic, and still answers its own question “are there any hidden fees?” with “No. All pricing is transparent and listed above”. It is also the only page where a fifth plan appears at all: a Plus Plan at $19.99 a month or $167.92 a year, for Shopify Plus merchants only, adding “the ability to show the checkbox in the actual Checkout page of your store”. The Plus Plan is the one rate that has not moved in any of our readings, so it now sits $7 above Pro. The article also notes that uninstalling during an ongoing billing period still incurs that period's charge.

Developer Effective Apps, trading as Effectify, at 13 Max Nordau, Ashdod, Israel; the app launched on 2 December 2019, carries Shopify's Built for Shopify badge, and stood at 565 listing reviews with a 4.9 average on 14 October 2026, up from 557 on 29 September and 550 on 9 September.

Re-read on 14 October 2026: the listing and the vendor's pricing article (updated 17 September 2026) show the same three monthly and annual rates as on 29 September, and the article still lists the Plus Plan at $19.99 a month or $167.92 a year.
